The blue-marked sections of the clock tree diagram in the datasheet are not applicable (they only apply to chips whose 5th lot-number digit is greater than 0).
GPHA, Ethernet, SerDes and CAN functions are not provided.

CH32L103K8U and CH32L103F8U6 have a built-in 5.1kΩ pull-down resistor that is forced on in standby mode; standby current increases by about 5uA and the pull-down configuration note in the datasheet is not needed.
The blue-dashed sections of the clock tree (Figure 2-4) are not applicable to these CH32V203RB lots (they only apply when the 5th-to-last lot digit is greater than 0).
CH32V203RB uses a 32MHz external crystal or clock (HSE); no load capacitors are needed with an external crystal as they are built in.
CAN and USBPD functions are not provided (applies to the products listed in CH32V205DS0, including CH32V203CCT6).

column4: SDIO_D0 and SDIO_D1 are mapped to PC8 and PC9 by default. For matching lots (except CH32V305GBU6), the default mapping automatically changes to PB14 and PB15 when bit[14]ETHMACEN=1 and bit[10]SDIOEN=1 in register RCC_AHBPCENR.

column4: SPI3_MOSI is mapped to PB5 by default. For matching lots, when Ethernet is used the I2S3 default pin functions and the SPI3 default chip-select are unavailable, and the SPI3_MOSI default mapping automatically changes to PA15.
V_IO supports a minimum supply voltage of 1.2V instead of 1.8V (products without an independent V_IO supply and CH32V305GBU6 excluded).
The non-zero-wait flash area additionally supports RVV instructions and 64-bit DMA access.
Current consumption is higher than the CH32V407 values in the datasheet tables: about +2~22mA in operating mode and +90uA in stop mode.
PSRAM supports clocks above 200MHz, variable and instruction access, and byte write; in stop mode (voltage regulator in low-power mode) PSRAM data is retained.
In stop mode with the voltage regulator in low-power mode, bit LDO18_EN in register PWR_CTLR must be configured to 0.
ADC channels 3, 7, 11 and 15, and the I2C function, are not available.
The PC10/PC17 and PC11/PC16 pin pairs are internally bonded together; both IOs of a pair must not be configured as outputs at the same time.
The blue-marked sections of the clock tree diagram in the datasheet are not applicable (they only apply to chips whose 5th lot-number digit is greater than 0).
